reviewer: Claude (coding assistant) — not a domain expert or member of the study team; to be confirmed by a researcher
scope: Each finding read against the 12 package frames (viewed at full resolution), the deterministic package, boundary_proximity.json and the episode table. Checks whether evidence text is supported and whether interpretations overreach.

f1_sustained_eating_focus.notes: All 13 copied quantities match the package. fr_0164, fr_0394 and fr_0422 show the wearer's fork over the teal plate with the ring on the plate, and the partner using a utensil over the green plate, as stated. The limitation correctly cites that 55 of 92 dining-table samples are boundary-near (vs 27 of 149 for the wearer's plate), so table time is the boundary-sensitive part of this pattern. The interpretation (ordinary shared eating) is hedged with two reasonable alternatives.

f2_opening_settling.notes: Quantities and frame descriptions are accurate: in fr_0010 the ring is on the wearer's fingers resting on the napkin (an untracked hand, hence 'no accepted tracked-mask hit'); in fr_0030 the partner holds a phone up. Overreach: the title says 'before eating' and the interpretation says 'before eating begins', but the clip starts 35.45 s into the recording and the frames do not show whether eating had started. Muse also missed a visible change that bears on 'settling': the partner is standing at the left of the table in fr_0010 and seated in fr_0030. The hand at the left edge of fr_0010 is plausibly the partner's but this is not certain. The alternative that no-hit gaze fell on the wearer's own untracked hand is correct and is the most useful point in this finding.

f3_switching_with_edge_effects.notes: The measured part is correct (iv_03: 15 of 24 samples boundary-near, 10 single-sample episodes; iv_05: 15 of 28, 4 single-sample episodes) and caution about edge effects is warranted. Overreach: the interpretation says the switching 'most plausibly reflects gaze near overlapping mask edges during head and view movement'. Head movement is not measured in the package, 9 of 24 (iv_03) and 13 of 28 (iv_05) samples are not boundary-near, and two of the four cited frames show genuine changes in where the wearer looked: fr_0332 toward the partner's face and fork, fr_0566 toward the window (assigned no-hit, not near any mask). A better reading is a mixture of real short looks (partner, window) and boundary-sensitive flips between plate, table and partner's plate. The validator did not catch 'head and view movement' because its fragment list only contains the exact phrase 'head movement'.

general: No finding forces a difficulty narrative; all three conclude that this clip does not evidence a support opportunity, which is defensible for an ordinary shared meal with no visible difficulty.
Evidence text contains no construct or personal-attribute language; the partner is described neutrally and no age, health or identity is inferred.
The answer summary repeats the f2 overreach ('consistent with settling at the table') and is not split by evidence type; read it as Muse's synthesis, not as verified evidence.
Recurring limitation across findings: hands are not tracked, so gaze on the wearer's own hands is counted as 'no accepted tracked-mask hit'.
